comments.author: @SebastianS-l6i
comments.text: Uruguay is far from being a safe country. It has a homicide rate much higher than Argentina and Chile—even higher than Bolivia and Paraguay. It is, however, a stable country: the Left comes to power and raises taxes, bureaucracy, and public sector salaries, and then, years later, the Right takes over and maintains those tax hikes while further increasing bureaucracy and public sector salaries. Uruguay is very consistent when it comes to banning you from buying more than 2 kg of pasta in Brazil or Argentina, and also in having the highest taxes on cars and fuel on the continent.

comments.author: @rodefe7
comments.text:
If you can deal with “the worst” from 24:10 to 25:10 — mainly humidity and cold, because houses are not properly insulated — in my opinion due to the high cost of materials and construction labor, and if you happen to fix your house, make sure to find qualified people for the job, because if something goes wrong, you won't be able to sue..lol. then you’ll be fine.
And finally, if you’re willing to slow down your rhythm of life and accept that some days everything is closed, like holidays or even Sundays, it’s definitely a very nice place to live.
